FLAGSHIP READ: As a reminder, the Strait of Hormuz has reverted back to a de facto closure as the US and Iran are engaging in military strikes once again.

And with that, the US has also reimposed their naval blockade at the other end of the strait.

As such, both sides have pretty much hit the reset button to the ceasefire deal/memorandum of understanding.

For the time being, the latest shiptracking data shows that traffic along the strait has gone back all the way down.

And by that, I mean to the lowest point during the peak of the conflict.

In terms of verified crossings, there are less than 10 ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz per day since 18 July.

And even if accounting for shadow fleet crossings, the numbers being reported aren't all too encouraging with that being around 13-19 vessels per day over the weekend.

Mind you, oil and gas shipments have pretty much hit a standstill as a result.

And that remains the number one caveat that ONS is pinning on their labour market report this month.

The headline estimate points to the UK jobless rate keeping steady in May at 4.9%.

So far this year, the figure is up 0.2% with UK economic inactivity rate estimated to have fallen by 0.1% year-to-date to 20.9%.

That matches up with the payrolls figure, which dipped again in June, dropping by 71,000 (0.2%) so far this year.

All in all, it still points to some softening in the UK labour market but not quite as pronounced to warrant immediate worries by the BOE.

Besides that, pay growth continues to show a bit of a divergence total pay keeping above 4% but regular pay holding at 3.4% after the continued dip since January.

In terms of real pay growth, total pay has bounced back to 1.1% from a low of 0.6% in the three months to February.
